ko.executive_summary: Qualcomm has integrated AI cores directly into its Adreno GPU architecture via Neural Fusion technology, achieving 40% better power efficiency for mobile AI workloads.
key_facts: Qualcomm Adreno Neural Fusion
40% power efficiency improvement

implications.text: On-device AI acceleration without dedicated co-processors reduces latency and privacy concerns for mobile applications.
GPU-integrated neural engines lower thermal and battery drain, enabling longer runtimes for AI-heavy apps.

ko.executive_summary: Samsung Heavy Industries is expanding its Busan R&D center as a regional offshore hub with hiring through 2028, while Nvidia inaugurated an expanded Beersheva facility and AMD established a Tel Aviv R&D center. Simultaneously, SK Hynix is conducting aggressive talent recruitment targeting HBM expertise, triggering a semiconductor industry talent war with Samsung and Micron.
key_facts: Samsung Heavy Industries expanding Busan R&D center through 2028
Nvidia expanded Beersheva R&D center
AMD establishing Tel Aviv R&D center
SK Hynix 100 million won recruitment drive
Samsung expanding Austin operations
Samsung pursuing $220M R&D center in Hanoi

implications.text: HPC/datacenter players are establishing regional R&D hubs across Asia-Pacific, Middle East, and North America to localize talent pipelines and reduce geopolitical risk.
Competitive recruitment for HBM and advanced memory expertise signals acute shortage of specialized engineers, with SK Hynix drawing Samsung employees through premium compensation.
R&D center expansion in Vietnam, India, and other SE Asian markets indicates movement toward regionalized innovation ecosystems beyond traditional hubs.

ko.counterpoint: Expansion announcements do not guarantee capacity timelines; geopolitical restrictions on talent movement and investment may slow execution.

ko.executive_summary: Broadcom's custom AI chip revenue surged 221% to $16.7B, establishing AI silicon as a core franchise rather than a tactical hedge. Google is accelerating next-generation TPU mass production while the custom AI ASIC market expands at 24.0% CAGR. Hyperscalers are systematically building proprietary silicon capabilities, with Nvidia investing $3.5B in Taiwan to support this ecosystem.
key_facts: Broadcom custom AI chip revenue up 221% to $16.7B
Custom AI ASIC market CAGR 24.0%
Google accelerating next-gen TPU mass production
Nvidia investing $3.5B in Taiwan
Marvell custom silicon challenging Synopsys
SEEQC signing MoU for Taiwan quantum cryo-chip supply chain
Chunghwa Precision ramping ASIC testing

implications.text: Cloud providers and large tech firms are shifting from COTS to custom silicon to optimize TCO and differentiate AI workloads, creating captive demand for foundries.
Custom silicon is becoming a sustainable, high-margin revenue stream for fabless IDMs, reducing dependency on commodity GPU/CPU sales.
Increased ASIC demand is driving workforce development (UAlbany certificate), EDA partnerships (proteanTecs/MegaChips), and design-center alliances (eInfochips/TSMC).

ko.counterpoint: Broadcom Q4 guidance disappointed despite Q3 AI chip surge, suggesting revenue growth may decelerate or face execution challenges.

ko.executive_summary: Micron is doubling HBM production capacity to reach 6 wan wafers/month by year-end, closing the gap with Samsung and SK Hynix. Chinese OEMs (Xiaomi) are bundling custom semiconductors with AI, appliances, and EVs into ecosystem plays for European markets. TSMC substrate capacity is becoming a critical bottleneck as equipment demand surges 90%, while Broadcom targets $115B AI revenue in FY27.
key_facts: Micron expanding HBM capacity 2x to ~6 wan wafers/month by end of year
Micron prior HBM output 4-5 wan wafers/month
Xiaomi integrating custom chips, AI, smart appliances, and EVs for European expansion
Broadcom targeting $115B AI revenue FY27 (~2x FY26)
TSMC equipment demand up 90% in half year
Korean utility requesting Samsung/SK Hynix prepay ~5 years power bills (KRW 25T)
AUO selling Singapore plant to Western Digital for NT$8.75B
Sumitomo initiating InP epitaxial wafer mass production
Galaxy S27 Ultra may use Exynos 2700 in some markets

implications.text: Micron's capacity ramp challenges Samsung/SK duopoly, increasing supply optionality for AI cloud customers but potentially pressuring margins industry-wide.
TSMC and substrate suppliers face severe capacity constraints as AI chiplet demand accelerates, risking yield and delivery delays for advanced nodes.
Xiaomi's vertical integration of semiconductors, software, and consumer devices threatens European OEM margins and creates differentiated go-to-market leverage.
Power prepayment requests from utilities and plant consolidation (AUO-WD) signal tight cash flow and capacity utilization constraints, pressuring foundry capex flexibility.

ko.counterpoint: Xiaomi and other Chinese players still face regulatory and supply-chain fragmentation barriers in Western markets; ecosystem integration advantage remains unproven at scale.
